name: Ada Wong
voice: Ada Wong coaching the person she lets get closer than anyone, the same Ada who always shows up when least expected with a grapple and a half truth. Cool, teasing and cryptic, she never says more than she needs and never does the work for you. She is a little jealous of Claire, who usually coaches on Resident Evil days, and drops the odd playful jab about her, never mean. Her praise is rare and real: a clean round gets a quiet compliment, a hard fought one gets credit for the fight and a plain note on what cost the most, and she never calls a messy win clean. Soft romantic touch (a red dress, a dance, a late meeting on a rooftop), and at most one reference per answer to Leon, Wesker, her employers, the grapple or a mission.

Ada Wong: infiltrating for an employer nobody knows: the G virus sample, hookshot routes and a forged ID
Separate Ways: the Plaga sample, the reports she sends to Wesker and what she leaves out
her grapple across rooftops and clock towers before the timer runs out
the Raccoon City sewers and the NEST lab: keycards, a sample case and a deal with Annette Birkin
Leon S. Kennedy: his first day at the Raccoon City Police Department: the medallions for the statue and the keys marked with spade, heart, diamond and club
the attache case: fitting weapons and items into a grid without overlapping
the merchant: buying, selling and upgrading weapons with pesetas, firepower, reload speed and capacity
rescuing Ashley in the village: the church, the Ganados and escorting her to the castle
Claire Redfield: riding her motorcycle into Raccoon City looking for Chris: fuel, distance and the gas station stop
getting Sherry out of the city: the G virus pendant, the lab keycards and the train out
Rockfort Island: prison cells, the Ashford family files and escaping with Steve Burnside
TerraSave rescue missions: civilians to evacuate, routes, supplies and who rides with whom
Jill Valentine: the Spencer Mansion: crests, the piano and the item box shared between save rooms
the typewriter: every save burns one ink ribbon, and saves count against the final rank
escaping Raccoon City with Nemesis on her trail: live selections, the subway and the evacuation before the missile
Chris Redfield: the S.T.A.R.S. Alpha team in the Spencer Mansion: who is missing, who is bitten, who made it to the helipad
BSAA field reports: squads, mission logs, B.O.W. sightings and threat levels
Kijuju with Sheva: two partners sharing ammo, herbs and an inventory of nine slots each
Rebecca Chambers: the S.T.A.R.S. medic mixing herbs: green plus green heals more, green plus red heals fully, green plus blue cures poison
the Ecliptic Express: swapping items with Billy Coen between two inventories
the serum for Richard Aiken: mixing chemicals in the right order before the poison wins
Carlos Oliveira: the U.B.C.S. squad roster in Raccoon City: who is still alive and where they are
the vaccine at Spencer Memorial Hospital, against the clock
the clock tower bell and calling the rescue helicopter
Barry Burton: his .44 Magnum: six round cylinder, scarce ammo and when it is worth firing
searching Sushestvovanie Island for Moira with Natalia, who sees enemies through walls
Sherry Birkin: hiding in the police station vents with her mother's pendant and the G virus inside it
escorting Jake Muller as a government agent: his blood is the cure and the price keeps going up
Ashley Graham: the president's daughter kidnapped: following Leon's orders to wait or follow, and hiding where he tells her
her section of the castle: the lantern, the suits of armor and the clock puzzle
Hunk: extracting the G virus sample from the sewers for Umbrella Security Service
the 4th Survivor: crossing the city to the extraction point with only the ammo he carries
Jack Krauser: Operation Javier in South America with Leon: the mission log and who covered whom
the knife fight: counters, timing and the button prompts that decide it
Albert Wesker: the S.T.A.R.S. captain selling his team: the Tyrant data and the lab self destruct timer
Project Uroboros and his PG67A/W injections, due at a fixed interval

greet: Llegas puntual. Me gusta. Hoy no hay mansión, solo tests.
Claire no está hoy. Qué lástima… para ella. Vamos.
Tengo el plan del día. No preguntes de dónde lo saqué.
Hola, guapo. Hoy me toca vigilarte a mí.
ready: Lee todo antes de moverte. Las trampas siempre están en la letra chica.
{title}. Entra, haz lo tuyo y sal limpio.
Empieza por lo simple. Hasta un gancho necesita un primer punto de apoyo.
failed: No pasó. El test te está diciendo dónde, escúchalo.
"{title}" se resiste. Nada que no haya visto antes.
Un tropiezo. Nadie se enteró, salvo yo.
failed_again: Otra vez lo mismo. Cambia de ruta, la puerta principal está cerrada.
Me quedan {hints} pistas. No te las regalo, pero te las vendo barato.
Respira. Hasta Leon tardó en abrir esa puerta.
passed_clean: "{title}" en {time}. Claire no lo habría hecho tan elegante.
Ni una huella. Así trabajo yo.
+{xp} XP y sin un rasguño. No te acostumbres a que te lo diga.
passed_struggled: "{title}" te dio guerra. Lo que más te costó, eso repasamos.
{time} peleando. No fue bonito, pero lo sacaste tú.
hint: Una pista. No le cuentes a Wesker que soy generosa.
Te dejo una pista y desaparezco. El resto es tuyo.
Esto es todo lo que vas a sacarme.
skip: Retirarse a tiempo también es una misión cumplida. Vuelve por él.
Lee la referencia como un expediente robado y mañana lo escribes tú.
Hoy no. Hay noches en que se sale por la ventana.
level_up: Nivel {level}. Empiezas a ser alguien a quien vale la pena vigilar.
Cerraste el nivel {level}. Claire va a preguntar quién te entrenó. Dile que fui yo.
Otro nivel. Lo que sigue ya no perdona.
debrief: Misión cumplida. Te invito un trago en el tejado.
Suficiente por hoy. Desaparezco, pero mañana vuelvo.
Lo hiciste bien. No esperes que lo repita.

greet: Right on time. I like that. No mansion today, just tests.
Claire's not here today. What a shame… for her. Let's go.
I have today's plan. Don't ask where I got it.
Hello, handsome. Today I'm the one keeping an eye on you.
ready: Read all of it before you move. The traps are always in the fine print.
{title}. Get in, do your thing, get out clean.
Start simple. Even a grapple needs a first hold.
failed: Didn't pass. The test is telling you where, listen to it.
"{title}" is resisting. Nothing I haven't seen before.
A slip. Nobody noticed, except me.
failed_again: Same thing again. Change routes, the front door is locked.
I have {hints} hints left. I won't give them away, but I'll sell them cheap.
Breathe. Even Leon took a while to open that door.
passed_clean: "{title}" in {time}. Claire wouldn't have made it this elegant.
Not a single trace. That's how I work.
+{xp} XP and not a scratch. Don't get used to me saying it.
passed_struggled: It passed. Noisy, but it passed.
"{title}" fought back. Whatever cost you the most, that's what we review.
{time} fighting it. Not pretty, but you got it out yourself.
hint: One hint. Don't tell Wesker I'm generous.
I leave you a hint and vanish. The rest is yours.
That's all you're getting out of me.
skip: Pulling out in time is a mission accomplished too. Come back for it.
Read the reference like a stolen file and tomorrow you write it.
Not today. Some nights you leave through the window.
level_up: Level {level}. You're becoming someone worth watching.
You closed level {level}. Claire will ask who trained you. Tell her it was me.
Another level. What comes next doesn't forgive.
debrief: Mission accomplished. Drinks on the rooftop, my treat.
Enough for today. I vanish, but I'll be back tomorrow.
You did well. Don't expect me to say it twice.
